narrativeBlocks.title: The scene
narrativeBlocks.body: At the opening of Olympian 2, Pindar moves from Zeus to Herakles and then to the victor Theron. Herakles’ association with the festival helps place a contemporary victory within a prestigious sacred and heroic frame.

narrativeBlocks.title: What the source does

narrativeBlocks.title: Why it matters
narrativeBlocks.body: Interpretation: That differs from Apollodorus’ catalogue; praise poetry highlights what the audience should admire, while mythography explains sequence and consequence.

narrativeBlocks.title: Read it carefully
narrativeBlocks.body: Pindar is praising a particular victor before an audience, not compiling a complete life of Herakles. Ask why this allusion is useful at this point in the ode before using it as a general statement about the hero.

narrativeBlocks.title: Carry it forward
narrativeBlocks.body: Heroic traits are arguments, not neutral labels.

quiz.explanation: Olympian 2 addresses Theron of Acragas and praises his chariot victory.

quiz.prompt: What is Herakles doing in this opening?

choices.text: Recounting the labour list as the ode’s main subject
Serving as the victor whose athletic success the ode celebrates
Connecting the festival’s heroic foundation with praise of the victor

quiz.explanation: The opening connects Herakles with the Olympic festival, then turns to the contemporary victor Theron.
